title: Pipeline TPS cartography — end-to-end microbenchmark framework for core models
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a reproducible microbenchmark framework that maps tokens-per-second (TPS) behavior across multidimensional workload axes (sequence length, batch size, KV warm/cold, concurrency, model variant) and produces p95 latency cartography and regression signals. The goal is a single CI-driven flow that runs lightweight probes on PRs, nightly full cartography sweeps, and bisection-friendly regression drilldowns with artifactized traces and dashboards.
comments: 2026-01-21 - Kickoff: scoped to core models (redwood-7b, redwood-13b, open-6.9b) and two hardware profiles (A100-80GB, H100). Agreed on cartography concept during sync: heatmaps + sliceable time series.

2026-01-30 - Spike complete: built a small WebAssembly-based synthetic client to emulate hundreds of concurrent request streams with exact token cadence. Found that Python runners add ~10% noise; benchmark runner will be Rust for stable tail noise.

2026-02-07 - Design decision: adopt a hybrid runner: Rust for the core TPS engine (deterministic timing, low jitter) + Go orchestration layer to integrate with CI/GitHub checks and secrets. Rationale: Rust gives stable microsecond timing; Go has existing infra libraries for our CI.

2026-02-20 - Data schema agreed: normalized CSV + ndjson trace artifacts and a small metadata Parquet summary per run. Results upload to s3://redwood-perf/cartography/<date>/<run-id> and hooked to Grafana via a Prometheus pushgateway shim for quick dashboards.

2026-02-27 - Implemented p95 drift detector prototype: compares baseline cartography heatmap to current run using Earth Mover's Distance over p95 slices. Prototype flagged 13% p95 drift on redwood-13b when quantization profile X was enabled — filed follow-up ENG-875431.

2026-03-05 - CI integration: created a lightweight PR check job (ci/perf/tps-smoke) that runs a 90s steady-state probe and posts results as a GitHub check. Example PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/core/pull/2486 has the perf-check annotation.

2026-03-10 - Reviewed by PM (Priya Singh): asked for customer-facing signal definitions and an SLA mapping doc. Added to attachments. Also requested a gradual rollout plan for using automated regression signals to block merges.

2026-03-12 - Engineering review: added a mechanism to replay exact token cadence for bisecting regressions and to annotate GitHub PRs with candidate commits. Draft PR for runner: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-runner/pull/52
attachments: Incident notes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/servicedesk/INC-2119 (related p95 regression during canary)
decisions: Use Rust for the microbenchmark engine to minimize host jitter and enable deterministic token cadence emulation.
Orchestrate via Go to reuse existing CI libraries and GitHub check integrations.
Store canonical run artifacts (ndjson traces + Parquet summaries) in S3 and surface aggregated metrics to Grafana via a pushgateway.
Implement p95 regression detection using distribution-aware distance metrics (EMD) rather than simple mean/p95 diffs to reduce false positives from tail sampling noise.
Expose an opt-in gating policy: automated signals appear in PRs but only block merges after human review + two sustained nightly confirmations.
Support both lightweight PR smoke runs (30–120s) and full cartography sweeps (hours) scheduled nightly.
Normalize results by cold vs warm KV cache and provide per-run metadata so slices are comparable.
Add synthetic microburst and jitter injection knobs to emulate real production traffic patterns.
Integrate with perf-bisector tooling to automatically create candidate bisect PRs when a regression is detected.
Ship initial MVP without multi-region routing; add region-dimensions in follow-ups if needed.

Complete Go orchestration layer: implement job templates and GitHub check uploader (ETA 2026-03-25).
